title: Metadata-only binary workflow to guarded task preview
request: Continue with TP-01D only: convert a validated basic binary classification workflow into an accurate, non-executing TaskGraph using existing source plans, project metadata and registered capabilities.
spec: engineering/planning/TP_01D.txt and the hierarchical planning master package; no new ML computation, project writes, approvals, UI, runtime defaults or later package implementation.
plan: Inspect current source owners and reuse the prior contracts, validators and registry.
Write failing adapter and safety tests; author a clearly labelled Telco metadata fixture.
Compile exact source coverage into existing physical stages and a separate human gate.
Bind source, project, dataset, capability and execution-context identities without copying values.
Run adversarial review, fix reproduced findings, deliver a generated preview and documentation.
Verify focused compatibility and applicable package gates before completion.

decisions.decision: Keep the adapter in dclab_rnd.tasks and reuse unchanged core contracts and validators.
decisions.why: This compiler binds R&D-specific project and registry metadata; putting host dependencies in the portable core would violate its dependency boundary.

decisions.decision: Accept supplied metadata and a detached capability snapshot, never a store or runtime context.
decisions.why: Planning must not load raw tables, fit, call tools or models, save a project or create human approvals.

decisions.decision: Read canonical registry schemas and require an explicit host allowlist and project guard.
decisions.why: Registry membership is not permission; copied local schemas or aliases could invent an unsupported execution path.

decisions.decision: Use one data action for class balance, holdout lock and training analysis; one final action for threshold selection and final evaluation.
decisions.why: These are the existing physical owners. Splitting them would duplicate training or holdout effects.

decisions.decision: Retain the required features action with no invented source step.
decisions.why: The studio engine needs that stage even though the abstract classification workflow has no generic feature step.

decisions.decision: Support the real portable plan projection and block extra unadopted solver decisions.
decisions.why: The engine does not implement every portable plan choice; it consumes saved threshold and label policies narrowly. A proposal cannot silently change the owner or claim adoption.

decisions.decision: Preserve the signed Solution hash and add an independent execution-context digest.
decisions.why: Human signature compatibility must remain intact, while sampling, packs, recipes and other actual execution inputs must invalidate stale graph identities.

decisions.decision: Use actual ProblemCard identity and existing final record paths.
decisions.why: Opaque references must name the right source type and evidence fields must exist on their declared owner.

decisions.decision: Return no graph when essential identity is absent; otherwise retain explicit blocked task diagnostics.
decisions.why: Inventing a dataset hash, capability or approval is unsafe. A blocked diagnostic graph is not admitted for readiness and preserves current core rejection rules.

decisions.decision: Use authored Telco metadata with explicitly synthetic digests and signoff.
decisions.why: It proves current builder/registry/contract integration without implying that a real table was opened or a real approval granted.

change: Adds the host adapter and registry snapshot helper, forty-one adapter tests, authored Telco metadata and an adapter-generated task preview. Documents exact source mapping, input identities, conservative unsupported scope and future runtime verification. Core remains 0.157.0 with the same contracts and schemas.

findings.defect: No supported workflow-to-task adapter existed in the current checkout.
findings.scenario: The first positive and failure-path suite could not import dclab_rnd.tasks.
findings.cause: Prior packages intentionally stopped at contracts and pure validation.
findings.fix: Add a metadata-only compiler with exact stage ownership and explicit blockers.
findings.test: Initial suite failed with ModuleNotFoundError; positive source builder and real registry tests now pass.

findings.defect: The first draft could compile a supplied plan while the saved runtime plan contained different threshold policies.
findings.scenario: A signed Solution stayed unchanged but project.plan added an expected-cost threshold policy unseen by the supplied source plan.
findings.cause: The existing signature covers Solution fields only; the first draft did not bind the separately consumed runtime plan.
findings.fix: Require exact source/runtime plan identity when present, retain its source hash, and block unadopted choices.
findings.test: The saved runtime-plan mismatch test failed before the change and now blocks all actions.

findings.defect: Initial mapping copied logical artifact names without linking them to existing owner records.
findings.scenario: A final step consumed the logical holdout without an explicit data_record reference in the mapping report.
findings.cause: Only node-level lineage was initially represented.
findings.fix: Add input/output artifact references without inventing separate training/holdout files or outputs for steps that declare none.
findings.test: Source artifact mapping tests failed on missing keys and now verify every required role.

findings.defect: Generic JSON Schema validation could implicitly fetch a referenced remote or local schema.
findings.scenario: A capability parameter used a remote or file reference during a supposedly non-executing preview.
findings.cause: The installed validator supports automatic reference retrieval.
findings.fix: Block all schema references before validation rather than allowing resolver I/O.
findings.test: A red test with a mocked retrieval function reproduced resolution; current tests verify zero retrieval attempts and blocked operations.

findings.defect: Sampling settings, effective pack and other owner-consumed context were absent from the graph identity.
findings.scenario: Changing quick/max_rows or an imbalanced pack initially retained the same mapped graph hash.
findings.cause: The first adapter bound Solution and dataset but overlooked separate preparation, recipe, threshold and disclosure inputs.
findings.fix: Hash an explicit metadata projection as a separate execution-context source and required input. Resolve the actual kind; block nonbasic programmes, splits, tables and unclassified sensitivity rather than reading values.
findings.test: Reviewer-context regressions failed before the change. Settings, pack fallback, feature programs, plan, brief, exposure, adopted changes, proposal modifiers, categorical and sensitivity metadata now affect identity or block appropriately.

findings.defect: A ProblemBrief digest was labelled as a ProblemCard source reference.
findings.scenario: Reading the referenced document as ProblemCard failed its contract.
findings.cause: The adapter reused the brief helper but labelled it with the available card reference kind.
findings.fix: Build the actual pure ProblemCard from the supplied brief metadata and hash that contract.
findings.test: A red test compared the source against the real ProblemCard reader and now passes.

findings.defect: The first mapping named a metrics field that does not exist on actual final stage records.
findings.scenario: A verifier following the suggested final evidence path would find no field.
findings.cause: Generic metric terminology was used instead of the existing record schema.
findings.fix: Use evidence.holdout_metrics, holdout_primary_metric_ci, holdout_consumed, holdout_uses_in_this_project and run.
findings.test: Final evidence path regression failed before the correction and now checks real field names.

findings.defect: A caller could omit execution settings and still receive a mapped preview.
findings.scenario: A sparse metadata projection hid the actual sampling/fold settings.
findings.cause: The first context projection hashed missing values without requiring the current settings object.
findings.fix: Require current settings metadata and block instead of guessing defaults; the fixture uses current pure project defaults.
findings.test: The dedicated missing-settings red test failed before the guard and now blocks all actions.

findings.defect: One new test used a Decision.source value outside the existing contract.
findings.scenario: The self-confirmation test failed during construction before reaching adapter logic.
findings.cause: The test used model instead of the existing advisor source enum.
findings.fix: Correct the fixture to the current advisor enum, without changing the contract or weakening the assertion.
findings.test: The corrected test reaches the adapter and confirms that model acceptance cannot replace human signoff.

findings.defect: Final regeneration damaged a generated training file with embedded NUL bytes, causing the development-corpus freshness check to fail.
findings.scenario: After make sft-dev exited successfully, train.chat.jsonl contained NUL bytes and differed from a clean build.
findings.cause: The producer of the byte damage was not established. The same class of generated-file damage had previously occurred before this adapter package; no adapter source test failed.
findings.fix: Run the existing devlog generator with its supported --out option in a separate temporary directory, validate every JSON/JSONL file, then atomically replace the published generated files and rerun freshness tests.
findings.test: The initial completion refresh ran four tests with one freshness failure. Rebuilding with the supported --out generator, validating all five files and atomically publishing them passed all four tests in 3.893 seconds; all files contained zero NUL bytes.
findings.open: The process that introduced the file damage remains unconfirmed; source generator behavior is outside this adapter package.

measurements.result: All 262 schema files were byte-identical to HEAD and registry count remained 107. No core Python contract file was changed.

measurements.result: make check-quick JOBS=3 passed. File backend: 264 tests in 22 files/units in 100.6 seconds, one existing NOOA skip. PostgreSQL: 55 tests in five files/units in 37.9 seconds, no skips. All ten gates and all five product flows passed. No new adapter test skipped. Preflight rd-gates also passed.
limits: The existing skipped NOOA module belongs to the isolated agent environment and is not claimed passed.
This package validates metadata planning only. No live-model or sealed benchmark run, new task persistence backend, runtime dispatch or product rollout was performed.
Runtime still owns ambient code/runner/routing identity, authenticated approvals, current bytes, attempts, concurrency, budgets and scientific guards.

measurements.name: Initial completion corpus refresh
measurements.gate: Completion records and generated development corpus must match the existing generator exactly, with all four validation/freshness tests passing.
measurements.result: Four tests ran in 4.612 seconds; one freshness test failed on embedded NUL bytes in train.chat.jsonl after make sft-dev.
measurements.next: Rebuild through the existing --out generator in a temporary directory, publish validated files atomically and rerun freshness.

measurements.name: Staged completion corpus repair
measurements.gate: Rebuilt files must parse as valid JSON/JSONL without NUL bytes, preserve generator bytes through atomic publication, and pass all four development-record/freshness tests.
measurements.result: All five generator files parsed, contained zero NUL bytes and retained their verified hashes after atomic replacement. All four development-record/freshness tests passed in 3.893 seconds.
limits: The process that introduced the earlier file damage remains unconfirmed. This repair publishes exact generator output and does not change the generator or adapter source.

outcome: TP-01D complete: the basic binary metadata adapter produces an accurate non-executing TaskGraph and mapping report using existing owners and real registry metadata. Forty-one adapter tests, 104 combined foundation tests, 249 focused compatibility tests, installed core wheel, unchanged schemas, final review and full applicable check-quick gate pass. The final generated-corpus corruption was repaired by staged generator output and verified atomic publication; all four freshness tests then passed. The damage origin remains unconfirmed. Core contracts, runtime owners, model purposes and app defaults are unchanged. TP-01E is ready for a separate package and has not started. Changes remain uncommitted with one proposed review commit. The unrelated pre-existing store catalog edit is preserved.
lessons: A signed Solution is not a signature over every separately stored threshold or execution policy.
Graph identity must include every supplied input that changes preparation, recipes or disclosure.
Do not let schema validation perform network or file resolution during planning.
Source references must match the actual contract type, and evidence paths must match real records.
Expected evidence and artifact declarations are obligations, not proof that work was done.
Keep blocked diagnostics visibly distinct from an admitted graph and from execution permission.
risks: A planner could mistake tool membership for permission or a mapped graph for completion.
Splitting existing atomic engine stages could duplicate the holdout read.
Incomplete source fingerprints could allow stale settings or policies to reuse old plans.
Opaque metadata could accidentally copy table previews or imply nonexistent evidence.
